findings.quote: The data points are clustered to the left of the line (area), in a region where the count/mass ratio is lower than what was determined from ground testing. This indicates then, that the mass of the average particle counted on-orbit is higher than that determined on Earth.
findings.about: The average particle counted in orbit is heavier than on Earth
findings.note: Sample Bags #1 to #3 in orbit (GMT 233, 2006) against the ground tests of May 2003.

findings.quote: This observation makes sense since, on-orbit, without gravity to drive settling, more of the larger particles from the dust sample should remain entrained.
findings.about: Without settling, more large dust particles stay airborne in orbit

findings.quote: It should be noted that, although the DAFT Impactor is designed to filter out the larger particles, it is only about 50% efficient; which implies that it is allowing a considerable number of larger particles to be drawn into the devices.
findings.about: The DAFT Impactor removes only about 50% of the large particles

findings.quote: The average mass (assuming a material density of water) is 2.5 E-12 grams, with a range from 2 – 3 E-12.
findings.about: Average mass per particle across the bags: 2.5E-12 g
findings.note: Sample Bags #1 to #3; density of water assumed.

findings.quote: The calculated average diameter is 1.65 micron, ranging from 1.56 – 1.7 micron.
findings.about: Average particle diameter across the bags: 1.65 micron
findings.note: Sample Bags #1 to #3; computed from the mass per particle with density 1 g/cm3.

findings.quote: Therefore, the net amount of sample delivered to the Sample Bags is about 25 milligrams.
findings.about: About 25 mg of dust reached each sample bag

findings.quote: It also shows that as the run time on the P-Trak is increasing, especially during Bag #3, the count/mass ratio is declining.
findings.about: Count/mass ratio fell as the P-Trak ran, especially in Bag #3 (possible particle build-up)

findings.quote: However when the Ptrak and Dusttrak were returned, the data sets were intact in their memory. The stored data reproduced the read downs very closely giving confidence to the earlier conclusions.
findings.about: The instruments' stored logs reproduced the voiced-down readings

findings.quote: The project team believes that the optimal reading range for the P-Trak is from 30,000 – 100,000 pt/cc (although the published range goes up to 500,000 pt/cc) and for the DustTrak; 20 – 80 mg/m3. Clearly, the latest data was within this range.
findings.about: Optimal P-Trak range 30,000 to 100,000 pt/cc (DustTrak 20 to 80 mg/m3); the bag data said to be within it
findings.note: Lower end of the P-Trak range the team calls optimal.
